concern.concern: Fact F4 attributes “v^i(v_j)=δij, and the dual basis spans V*” to def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional. That supplier only defines linear functionals and the algebraic dual with pointwise operations; it does not state the finite dual-basis theorem. owner_review.reason: The actual published supplier only defines functionals and the full algebraic dual; it contains no dual-family or spanning theorem. The given two-vector basis supplies an immediate local derivation by linearity. Making that derivation explicit repairs the attribution without adding a supplier or changing the example interface.

proposed_edits.proposed_replacement: [F4] [[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]] defines $V^*$ as the space of linear functionals. Here the given dual coordinates are $v^0(av_0+bv_1)=a$ and $v^1(av_0+bv_1)=b$, so $v^i(v_j)=\delta_{ij}$. For $f\in V^*$, linearity gives $f(av_0+bv_1)=af(v_0)+bf(v_1)$, hence $f=f(v_0)v^0+f(v_1)v^1$ and these two functionals span $V^*$.
